_note: THE COMPOSER RESULT VOCABULARY (parity F13). `dsx.module.compose.{sms,mail}` PRESENT the system composer prefilled and never send: the user reads the message in their own messaging or mail app and taps send there. That is why no permission is involved on any renderer, and why no SEND_SMS row exists anywhere in this module. What this corpus exists to pin is the RESULT LADDER. iOS MessageUI reports exactly what the user did; Android's ACTION_SENDTO has no result callback at all and a browser's mailto: link has none either, so both report `unknown`. `unknown` must never be upgraded to `sent` because the intent launched: a caller that cannot trust `sent` has no reason to read the field. Runners: TS (@despia/kernel compose-core.ts, compose-conformance.test.ts), Kotlin (:core ComposeCore, ComposeConformanceTest), Swift (Engine/iOS/ComposeCore.swift, ComposeConformance in the record lane).

resultFidelity._note: renderer -> the results it can actually report. A renderer must never resolve a result outside its own list, and `saved` is a mail-draft outcome only.

permissionSurface._note: Every action on every renderer: none. This row is the contract. An SMS permission appearing in the merged manifest is a build regression, not a feature.

cases.name: a composer that reports the user's send says sent
a composer that reports a dismissal says cancelled, and it is not an error
a mail draft is its own outcome, distinct from both send and dismiss
a composer that reports a failure says failed
THE RULE: an intent-based composer reports unknown, never sent
the same for mail
a link-based composer reports unknown too
a launch that throws is no_composer, which is a different answer from unknown
an HTML body on a composer that cannot render it says isHtml:false rather than shipping markup as text
an HTML body on a composer that CAN render it carries no degradation flag

capabilities._note: Ask before offering the button. `defaultMailClient` is present only where the platform discloses it: Android names the resolving package, iOS never does, and a browser cannot observe whether a handler exists at all.

cases.name: a phone with both
a tablet with no SIM cannot text
a simulator has neither
Android names the resolving package
the Android resolver disambiguation activity is not a real client
a page can only promise that a composer may be ATTEMPTED

recipients._note: The cap is config (`max_recipients`, default 100), because no platform constant exists and clients truncate silently somewhere past a few dozen. A composer that opens with half the list is worse than one that refuses.

cases.name: under the cap opens
exactly the cap opens
over the cap refuses rather than truncating
mail counts to + cc + bcc together
no recipients at all is legal: the composer opens with an empty field

attachments._note: Local files only. A file that cannot be prepared is attachment_failed, never a composer that opens quietly missing it.

cases.name: a local file under the FileProvider roots attaches
a file outside the declared roots refuses
a missing file refuses
a remote URL is not fetched on the caller's behalf
the web cannot attach at all, and says so
